units.title: Number sense and arithmetic
units.subject: Mathematics
units.scope: Integers; factors; HCF/LCM; fractions; decimals; percentages; ratios; proportions; units; powers; roots; estimation
units.outcome: Explain why fraction algorithms work, estimate before calculating, and solve unfamiliar ratio and unit problems without a calculator.
units.notes: Do not begin calculus until algebra, functions, graphs and trigonometry survive a delayed mixed test.

units.title: Measurement matter and motion
units.subject: Science
units.scope: Measurements and uncertainty; matter; atoms; elements; mixtures; forces; motion; work and energy
units.outcome: Keep a measurement notebook, graph observations, distinguish evidence from inference, and balance units.
units.notes: No advanced quantum or device models before mechanics, waves, fields and relevant calculus.

units.title: Computer literacy and first Python
units.subject: Programming
units.scope: CPU RAM storage I/O; files folders processes; browser and internet; passwords updates backups; algorithms; expressions conditions loops
units.outcome: Organize and recover files, explain the parts of a computer, and write tested small programs from a blank file.
units.notes: No frameworks before functions, data, files, tests and independent debugging.

units.title: English reading and learning practice
units.subject: Communication
units.scope: Diagnostic grammar repair; comprehension; vocabulary from context; summaries; notes; error log; retrieval practice
units.outcome: Summarize a one-page explanation faithfully and give a two-minute oral explanation without copying.
units.notes: Do not use fluent AI prose to hide weak comprehension; explain claims in your own words.

units.title: Elementary algebra geometry and data
units.subject: Mathematics
units.scope: Variables; equations; inequalities; coordinates; angles; area; volume; graphs; mean median spread; elementary probability and logic
units.outcome: Translate a word problem into algebra, check a solution, and justify geometric and statistical claims.
units.notes: Do not begin calculus until algebra, functions, graphs and trigonometry survive a delayed mixed test.

units.title: Heat waves electricity and chemical change
units.subject: Science
units.scope: Heat and temperature; sound and light; simple circuits; magnetism; molecules; reactions; separation; conservation
units.outcome: Predict and explain low-voltage circuit observations and distinguish physical change from chemical change.
units.notes: No advanced quantum or device models before mechanics, waves, fields and relevant calculus.

units.title: Python problem solving and small utilities
units.subject: Programming
units.scope: Functions; strings; lists; dictionaries; files; exceptions; debugging; tests; decomposition; binary hexadecimal and Unicode
units.outcome: Build a file/text utility with input validation, tests and recovery from malformed data.
units.notes: No frameworks before functions, data, files, tests and independent debugging.

units.title: Technical explanation and scientific reasoning
units.subject: Communication
units.scope: Paragraph structure; technical vocabulary; diagrams; claims and evidence; source literacy; presentations
units.outcome: Write a reproducible experiment report and defend what its data do and do not establish.
units.notes: Do not use fluent AI prose to hide weak comprehension; explain claims in your own words.

units.title: Algebra functions geometry and trigonometry
units.subject: Mathematics
units.scope: Polynomials; factorization; simultaneous equations; functions; coordinate geometry; trig identities; logarithms; exponentials; sequences
units.outcome: Move fluently among equations, tables and graphs; solve trigonometric and exponential modelling problems.
units.notes: Do not begin calculus until algebra, functions, graphs and trigonometry survive a delayed mixed test.

units.title: Mechanics waves and thermal physics
units.subject: Physics
units.scope: Vectors; kinematics; Newton laws; gravitation; momentum; energy; oscillations; waves; thermodynamics
units.outcome: Construct free-body diagrams, state idealizations, and test conservation-law models with measurements.
units.notes: No advanced quantum or device models before mechanics, waves, fields and relevant calculus.

units.title: Chemical structure and quantitative chemistry
units.subject: Chemistry
units.scope: Atomic structure; periodicity; bonding; mole; stoichiometry; gases; solutions; thermochemistry
units.outcome: Balance reactions, calculate material quantities and explain the connection between bonding and properties.
units.notes: Do not pursue synthetic chemistry; repair moles, bonding and energy before electrochemistry/materials.

units.title: Python algorithms and modular programs
units.subject: Programming
units.scope: Recursion; searching sorting; simple classes; modules; data representations; test design; timing
units.outcome: Implement small algorithms, distinguish measured timing from complexity, and refactor a tested program.
units.notes: No frameworks before functions, data, files, tests and independent debugging.

units.title: Academic reading writing and argument
units.subject: Communication
units.scope: Technical reading; documentation search; evidence tables; citations; oral argument; basic literature search
units.outcome: Compare two explanations, trace a factual claim to its source and write an evidence-based technical argument.
units.notes: Do not use fluent AI prose to hide weak comprehension; explain claims in your own words.

units.title: Precalculus vectors matrices and proof
units.subject: Mathematics
units.scope: Permutations combinations; probability statistics; vectors matrices; limits derivatives integrals preview; sets relations logic induction
units.outcome: Solve a mixed readiness exam and prove simple statements by induction, contradiction and counterexample.
units.notes: Do not begin calculus until algebra, functions, graphs and trigonometry survive a delayed mixed test.

units.title: Electricity magnetism optics and modern physics
units.subject: Physics
units.scope: Fields potential circuits; induction; optics; photons; atomic models; semiconductors
units.outcome: Explain what circuit models omit and connect fields, photons and semiconductor behavior to devices.
units.notes: No advanced quantum or device models before mechanics, waves, fields and relevant calculus.

units.title: Equilibrium electrochemistry and materials foundations
units.subject: Chemistry
units.scope: Equilibrium; acid base; redox; electrochemistry; organic functional groups; inorganic materials; polymers
units.outcome: Explain batteries, corrosion and material selection quantitatively at school level.
units.notes: Do not pursue synthetic chemistry; repair moles, bonding and energy before electrochemistry/materials.

units.title: C introduction and memory reasoning
units.subject: Programming
units.scope: Compilation; functions; arrays; structures; pointers; stack and heap; ownership concept; modular files; tests
units.outcome: Draw memory diagrams, diagnose bounds and lifetime errors and implement a small modular C program.
units.notes: No unsafe concurrent systems before memory, lifetime, compiler diagnostics and debugger competence.

units.title: Linux shell Git and engineering workflow
units.subject: Software engineering
units.scope: Terminal; permissions; pipes; process tools; Git commits branches review; README; reproducible build; backups
units.outcome: Recreate a project on a fresh environment and explain each command and change.
units.notes: No unsafe concurrent systems before memory, lifetime, compiler diagnostics and debugger competence.

units.title: Single variable calculus
units.subject: Mathematics
units.scope: Limits continuity; derivatives; integration; series; Taylor approximation; modelling
units.outcome: Derive and solve calculus problems and estimate approximation error.
units.notes: No optimization shortcuts before derivatives, gradients, chain rule and approximation error.

units.title: Engineering physics and measurement
units.subject: Physics
units.scope: Calculus mechanics; oscillations; field models; optics; quantum and solid-state overview; uncertainty
units.outcome: Fit a physical model, propagate uncertainty and explain the assumptions limiting its use.
units.notes: No advanced quantum or device models before mechanics, waves, fields and relevant calculus.

units.title: Engineering chemistry and materials
units.subject: Chemistry
units.scope: Structure; thermodynamics; electrochemistry; corrosion; polymers; electronic materials; energy; environmental chemistry
units.outcome: Choose materials and power-storage options using properties, lifetime, environmental and cost constraints.
units.notes: Do not pursue synthetic chemistry; repair moles, bonding and energy before electrochemistry/materials.

units.title: Engineering graphics CAD and workshop literacy
units.subject: Graphics/CAD
units.scope: Geometric construction; orthographic isometric sections; dimensioning tolerances; 2D and 3D CAD; manufacturing and assembly literacy
units.outcome: Produce and interpret a dimensioned sensor enclosure drawing and verify fit with measurements.
units.notes: No complex assemblies before consistent projections, sections, dimensioning and fit checks.

units.title: C programming and software construction
units.subject: Programming
units.scope: Pointers ownership; dynamic allocation; ADTs; modular interfaces; compilation linking; debugging; test automation
units.outcome: Build and debug a memory-safe-by-discipline C application with an explicit allocation policy.
units.notes: No unsafe concurrent systems before memory, lifetime, compiler diagnostics and debugger competence.

units.title: Discrete mathematics and proof I
units.subject: Theory
units.scope: Propositional and predicate logic; sets functions relations; induction; invariants; counting
units.outcome: Write valid proofs and counterexamples and connect invariants to programs.
units.notes: No advanced algorithms before proof, recurrence, invariant and graph reasoning.

units.title: Engineering design and technical communication
units.subject: Professional practice
units.scope: Requirements; constraints; alternatives; design records; economics; ethics; evidence; review; team simulation
units.outcome: Deliver an original requirements-to-test design dossier and justify a rejected alternative.
units.notes: No deployment or safety claim without requirements, risk analysis, verification, validation and maintenance evidence.

units.title: Linear algebra
units.subject: Mathematics
units.scope: Elimination; vector spaces; linear maps; orthogonality; least squares; eigenvalues; SVD
units.outcome: Derive a least-squares solution and explain numerical and geometric meaning.
units.notes: No serious ML/graphics until maps, bases, least squares, eigenvalues and SVD are understood.

units.title: Multivariable calculus differential equations and modelling
units.subject: Mathematics
units.scope: Partials; gradients; Jacobians; multiple integrals; first and second order ODE; complex exponentials
units.outcome: Model coupled quantities and check a numerical solution against analytic special cases.
units.notes: No optimization shortcuts before derivatives, gradients, chain rule and approximation error.

units.title: Electrical circuits signals and measurement
units.subject: Electrical
units.scope: KCL KVL; DC AC; capacitors inductors; RC RL transients; transformers concept; instrumentation; sampling introduction
units.outcome: Predict and measure a low-voltage circuit, quantify disagreement, and select suitable instrument ranges.
units.notes: No live mains work. Device labs follow the first six weeks of circuit and instrument skills.

units.title: Electronics and sensor interfaces
units.subject: Electronics
units.scope: Diodes; BJT MOSFET; bias; op-amps; amplifiers; ADC DAC; sensors; datasheets; U028 first six weeks before device labs
units.outcome: Design and characterize a low-voltage sensor interface using measured limits.
units.notes: No RF or power electronics before low-voltage bias, loading, device limits and measurement.

units.title: Digital logic and simple CPU construction
units.subject: Digital logic
units.scope: Boolean algebra; gates; combinational logic; sequential logic; FSM; registers; ALU; RAM; CPU; HDL
units.outcome: Build and test gates through a small CPU in simulation and trace one instruction.
units.notes: No pipeline/FPGA complexity before gates, state, reset, registers, ALU and correct CPU simulation.

units.title: Data structures and C++ concepts
units.subject: Algorithms
units.scope: Lists; stacks queues; trees hash tables; graphs; asymptotic analysis; RAII; templates limited to containers
units.outcome: Implement, test and benchmark core data structures and explain invariants.
units.notes: No advanced algorithms before proof, recurrence, invariant and graph reasoning.

units.title: Sensor enclosure and data logger design
units.subject: Engineering design
units.scope: Integrated design using staged U028 U029 U030 skills; tolerance stack; interfaces; calibration
units.outcome: Deliver a functioning or explicitly simulated logger with CAD, circuit, firmware and measured acceptance tests.
units.notes: No deployment or safety claim without requirements, risk analysis, verification, validation and maintenance evidence.

units.title: Algorithms and discrete mathematics II
units.subject: Algorithms
units.scope: Sorting; graph algorithms; greedy; dynamic programming; recurrences; combinatorics; graph proofs
units.outcome: Design an algorithm, prove correctness and complexity, and compare implementation behavior.
units.notes: No advanced algorithms before proof, recurrence, invariant and graph reasoning.

units.title: Probability statistics and numerical computing
units.subject: Mathematics
units.scope: Conditional probability; random variables; expectation; distributions; estimation; testing; resampling; conditioning; floating point; roots integration; transforms introduction
units.outcome: Choose a probability model, quantify uncertainty and detect a numerically unstable computation.
units.notes: No empirical research claims without sampling, uncertainty, leakage and numerical-error literacy.

units.title: Computer organization architecture and assembly
units.subject: Architecture
units.scope: RISC-V; ISA; assembly ABI; datapath control; pipelines; caches; virtual-memory hardware; I/O; interrupts
units.outcome: Trace compiled code, build an emulator and measure cache and instruction effects.
units.notes: No advanced out-of-order mechanisms before ISA, ABI, datapath, pipeline hazards and cache models.

units.title: Relational databases and SQL
units.subject: Databases
units.scope: Relational model algebra; SQL; schemas; normalization; transactions ACID; indexes; query plans
units.outcome: Design a normalized schema, express nontrivial queries and explain transactions under concurrency.
units.notes: No distributed database internals before relational design, transactions, storage and OS concurrency.

units.title: Programming languages and functional programming
units.subject: Programming languages
units.scope: OCaml or Racket; immutable data; algebraic types; recursion; modules; semantics; evaluation; type rules
units.outcome: Implement an evaluator and compare language design choices.
units.notes: No optimizations before formal grammar, binding, semantics, types and observable behavior.

units.title: Systems construction studio
units.subject: Engineering design
units.scope: Allocator; CPU emulator; relational experiments; staged with U035 U036; requirements and measurements
units.outcome: Defend a systems implementation using invariants, memory tests and controlled benchmarks.
units.notes: No deployment or safety claim without requirements, risk analysis, verification, validation and maintenance evidence.

units.title: Operating systems
units.subject: OS
units.scope: Processes threads; scheduling; synchronization; deadlocks; virtual memory; filesystems; I/O; calls; protection; virtualization containers
units.outcome: Modify and debug a teaching kernel and explain isolation and persistence invariants.
units.notes: No serious distributed systems before processes, synchronization, virtual memory and filesystems.

units.title: Computer networks
units.subject: Networks
units.scope: Ethernet; switching; IPv4 IPv6; ARP DHCP DNS; UDP TCP; congestion control; routing; wireless; HTTP TLS; sockets; troubleshooting
units.outcome: Explain a captured request end to end and build a correctly framed network protocol.
units.notes: No advanced networking/security before packet traces, IP, TCP, DNS, HTTP, TLS and socket framing.

units.title: Automata computability and complexity
units.subject: Theory
units.scope: Automata; regular and context-free languages; Turing machines; decidability; reductions; P NP; NP-completeness
units.outcome: Construct machines and reductions and distinguish undecidability from computational hardness.
units.notes: No complexity research or mechanized verification before reductions and valid mathematical proofs.

units.title: Software engineering and web foundations
units.subject: Software engineering
units.scope: Requirements; contracts; OO design; tests; build dependency management; review; HTTP-first web; JS then TypeScript; authentication authorization; deployment rollback
units.outcome: Operate a tested small service with clear requirements, security boundaries and rollback.
units.notes: No framework specialization before HTTP, data modelling, tests, security boundaries and independent service delivery.

units.title: Interpreter and compiler front end
units.subject: Compilers
units.scope: Lexing; parsing; AST; semantic analysis; type checking; interpreter; study U041 grammars before parser theory
units.outcome: Build a language front end with precise error reporting and negative tests.
units.notes: No optimizations before formal grammar, binding, semantics, types and observable behavior.

units.title: Shell network service and team delivery
units.subject: Engineering design
units.scope: Shell; sockets; database integration; code review; trace across kernel network and storage; staged U039 U040 U042
units.outcome: Deliver an original integrated system and diagnose injected failures across layers.
units.notes: No deployment or safety claim without requirements, risk analysis, verification, validation and maintenance evidence.

units.title: Distributed systems foundations
units.subject: Distributed systems
units.scope: Time; partial failure; RPC; consistency; replication; consensus; partitioning; transactions; failure models
units.outcome: Implement and test a small replicated service under crash and partition faults.
units.notes: No consensus work before OS, networking, concurrency and explicit failure models.

units.title: Classical artificial intelligence
units.subject: AI/ML
units.scope: Search; heuristics; planning; constraints; knowledge representation; probabilistic inference; decision making
units.outcome: Implement search and probabilistic inference and assess failure cases.
units.notes: No DL/NLP/CV/RL depth before linear algebra, probability, optimization, algorithms and evaluation.

units.title: Machine learning and optimization
units.subject: AI/ML
units.scope: Regression; classification; trees; regularization; evaluation; clustering; PCA; gradient methods; generalization
units.outcome: Derive a basic learner, implement it and evaluate with leakage-resistant splits.
units.notes: No DL/NLP/CV/RL depth before linear algebra, probability, optimization, algorithms and evaluation.

units.title: Security and cryptographic foundations
units.subject: Security
units.scope: Threat models; OS network web security; auth; secure programming; crypto primitives; number theory; privacy; incident response
units.outcome: Threat-model and harden an owned service and explain why primitive choice alone does not make it secure.
units.notes: No advanced cryptography before discrete proof, probability and number theory; all security labs remain sandboxed.

units.title: Embedded systems and real-time foundations
units.subject: Embedded
units.scope: Embedded C; memory-mapped I/O; interrupts; timers; sensors; I2C SPI UART; RTOS; timing; embedded Linux concepts
units.outcome: Build and measure a timing-constrained device or explicitly scoped simulator.
units.notes: No safety-critical claim from a hobby prototype; interrupts and timing follow circuits, C, architecture and OS.

units.title: Research methods and experimental design
units.subject: Research
units.scope: Literature search; source hierarchy; hypotheses; experimental controls; reproducibility; statistics; benchmarks; ethics
units.outcome: Produce a small literature matrix and a reproducible baseline experiment.
units.notes: Choose one track after Year 3. No L6 claim before a bounded investigation survives external review.

units.title: Compiler back end and runtime systems
units.subject: Compilers
units.scope: IR; control/data flow; optimization; register allocation; code generation; runtime; garbage collection
units.outcome: Extend the front end into a compiler and prove or test transformation preconditions.
units.notes: No optimizations before formal grammar, binding, semantics, types and observable behavior.

units.title: Database internals and data architecture
units.subject: Databases
units.scope: Pages buffer pools; B+ trees; execution optimization; concurrency; logging recovery; distributed DB; NoSQL; warehouses; caching
units.outcome: Implement and fault-test selected storage and recovery components.
units.notes: No distributed database internals before relational design, transactions, storage and OS concurrency.

units.title: Parallel computing and performance
units.subject: Parallel/HPC
units.scope: Concurrency; parallel algorithms; SIMD threads; OpenMP; GPU concepts; coherence; scaling; profiling
units.outcome: Measure scaling with overhead, correctness and memory behavior accounted for.
units.notes: No GPU-scale investment before race-free CPU parallelism, profiling, locality and scaling evidence.

units.title: Computer graphics and HCI
units.subject: Graphics/HCI
units.scope: Rasterization; transformations; sampling; ray tracing; usability; accessibility; prototyping; user evaluation
units.outcome: Build a renderer and validate an interface with a documented evaluation protocol.
units.notes: No advanced rendering before linear algebra, geometry and sampling; no user study before consent and task design.

units.title: Formal methods and verification
units.subject: Theory
units.scope: Hoare logic; invariants; transition systems; model checking; proof assistant; type safety introduction
units.outcome: Prove a small program property and find a counterexample to a flawed protocol.
units.notes: No complexity research or mechanized verification before reductions and valid mathematical proofs.

units.title: Modern AI breadth and specialization exploration
units.subject: Specialization
units.scope: DL NLP CV RL generative-model survey; information theory; two short track samples; no new full course
units.outcome: Select one track based on prerequisite evidence, sustained work and a bounded question.
units.notes: No DL/NLP/CV/RL depth before linear algebra, probability, optimization, algorithms and evaluation.

units.title: Engineering delivery and cumulative review
units.subject: Engineering design
units.scope: Maintenance; reliability; accessibility; sustainability; deployment; incident drill; comprehensive core review
units.outcome: Repair a system from an unfamiliar bug report and defend the whole engineering lifecycle.
units.notes: No deployment or safety claim without requirements, risk analysis, verification, validation and maintenance evidence.

units.title: Advanced algorithms and complexity
units.subject: Algorithms
units.scope: Randomization; approximation; amortized analysis; advanced data structures; lower bounds; selected complexity
units.outcome: Solve unfamiliar problems and state the limits of an algorithmic guarantee.
units.notes: No advanced algorithms before proof, recurrence, invariant and graph reasoning.

units.title: Advanced systems and architecture
units.subject: Architecture
units.scope: Advanced OS; virtualization; advanced networking; coherence; branch prediction; out-of-order execution; accelerators; resource control
units.outcome: Measure one systems bottleneck and justify a cross-layer design choice.
units.notes: No advanced out-of-order mechanisms before ISA, ABI, datapath, pipeline hazards and cache models.

units.title: Primary specialization I
units.subject: Specialization
units.scope: One track core advanced text/course/lab; specialization prerequisites mandatory
units.outcome: Complete a substantial advanced assignment and critically read specialist papers.
units.notes: Choose one track after Year 3. No L6 claim before a bounded investigation survives external review.

units.title: Research reproduction I
units.subject: Research
units.scope: Select accessible paper and artifact; establish baseline; reproduce central result; record deviations
units.outcome: Produce a runnable reproduction with an uncertainty-aware comparison to the paper.
units.notes: Choose one track after Year 3. No L6 claim before a bounded investigation survives external review.

units.title: Advanced engineering design and project planning
units.subject: Engineering design
units.scope: Stakeholders; trade studies; reliability budgets; security design; engineering economics; test strategy
units.outcome: Submit a reviewed capstone specification, alternatives analysis and feasibility prototype.
units.notes: No deployment or safety claim without requirements, risk analysis, verification, validation and maintenance evidence.

units.title: Primary specialization II
units.subject: Specialization
units.scope: Graduate-level selected topics; advanced labs; one open-source subsystem
units.outcome: Solve an unfamiliar design problem and explain why competing approaches fail.
units.notes: Choose one track after Year 3. No L6 claim before a bounded investigation survives external review.

units.title: Advanced software engineering and operations
units.subject: Software engineering
units.scope: Reliability; observability; incident command; release; rollback; migration; technical debt; team review; advanced secure architecture
units.outcome: Run a realistic deployment, backup restoration and incident exercise.
units.notes: No framework specialization before HTTP, data modelling, tests, security boundaries and independent service delivery.

units.title: Research reproduction II
units.subject: Research
units.scope: Ablation; parameter sensitivity; competing baseline; statistical analysis; artifact packaging
units.outcome: Defend a replication report that separates reproduction failure from a refuted claim.
units.notes: Choose one track after Year 3. No L6 claim before a bounded investigation survives external review.

units.title: Capstone prototype and external design review
units.subject: Engineering design
units.scope: End-to-end prototype; one original deep mechanism; failure injection; independent reviewer feedback
units.outcome: Demonstrate feasibility and revise requirements using measured evidence.
units.notes: No deployment or safety claim without requirements, risk analysis, verification, validation and maintenance evidence.

units.title: Graduate mathematics gap repair
units.subject: Mathematics
units.scope: Track-specific proof probability analysis algebra or numerical gaps
units.outcome: Pass prerequisite problems for the selected graduate course.
units.notes: No empirical research claims without sampling, uncertainty, leakage and numerical-error literacy.

units.title: Graduate specialization seminar
units.subject: Specialization
units.scope: One graduate text/course segment; 8-12-paper seminar; critical synthesis
units.outcome: Explain current open problems with precise scope and defensible source evidence.
units.notes: Choose one track after Year 3. No L6 claim before a bounded investigation survives external review.

units.title: Independent engineering system I
units.subject: Engineering design
units.scope: Implement deep subsystem; integration; security; performance; operations; review
units.outcome: Deliver a usable alpha meeting baseline functional and fault-tolerance requirements.
units.notes: Choose one track after Year 3. No L6 claim before a bounded investigation survives external review.

units.title: Bounded research investigation I
units.subject: Research
units.scope: Question; related work; method; predeclared metrics; baseline; pilot; reproducibility
units.outcome: Defend a feasible research proposal and demonstrate a pilot result.
units.notes: Choose one track after Year 3. No L6 claim before a bounded investigation survives external review.

units.title: Professional review and independent practice
units.subject: Professional practice
units.scope: Independent debugging; external review; open-source contribution where feasible; technical presentations; cost and sustainability
units.outcome: Respond to substantive review and maintain a change and decision log.
units.notes: No deployment or safety claim without requirements, risk analysis, verification, validation and maintenance evidence.

units.title: Independent engineering system II
units.subject: Engineering design
units.scope: Hardening; adversarial tests; load; restore; upgrades; documentation; maintenance handover
units.outcome: Operate and defend a substantial system under specified failures and workload.
units.notes: Choose one track after Year 3. No L6 claim before a bounded investigation survives external review.

units.title: Graduate and professional transition

units.outcome: Identify realistic next programs or roles and document remaining mathematical or practical gaps.
